_provenance: HAND-AUTHORED FROM THE PINNED UPSTREAM SCHEMA. This is NOT a capture.
Transcribed from codex upstream tag rust-v0.151.0 — the exact version of the
binary this box spawns (~/.codex/packages/standalone/current/codex-package.json
-> 0.151.0). No codex turn was run to produce it: the only machine available
here is production, and #1255 forbids running real turns on it. Same posture,
and the same honesty requirement, as tests/fixtures/turn_plan_updated.json.
Shape: { threadId, turnId, tokenUsage: { total, last, modelContextWindow } },
where `total` and `last` are both TokenUsageBreakdown:
{ totalTokens, inputTokens, cachedInputTokens, cacheWriteInputTokens,
outputTokens, reasoningOutputTokens }.
`cacheWriteInputTokens` carries a serde default upstream, so a real frame may
omit it; it is written out here because a fixture that exercises the full
breakdown is more useful than one that exercises the default.
`modelContextWindow` is Option<i64> and serializes as an explicit null.
READ THIS BEFORE USING THE NUMBERS. `total` is a LIFETIME sum over every
response in the thread; `last` is the most recent single response. The numbers
below are chosen to make that impossible to ignore: total.totalTokens is
1400000 against a 272000 window — 5.1x over — while last.totalTokens is 60000,
or about 18.5% occupancy after the 12000-token baseline adjustment. Any code
that renders ~535% is dividing by the wrong field. Do not 'fix' the fixture to
make total smaller; a total several times the window is the ordinary state of a
long thread, and this file is the regression evidence for it.
`threadId` here is a PLACEHOLDER and is not part of the transcription. The
kernel's `on_notification` prologue drops any notification whose `threadId` is
not the harness's current thread, so the test substitutes its own seeded id
over this value before emitting the frame. Changing the literal below changes
nothing.
This becomes a real capture the moment the arm this fixture tests runs against
a live thread: the value lands in `worker_sessions.handle_state` under
`token_usage`, and `GET /api/cards/{id}/spec/run` reads it back. Note that the
stored value is the DERIVED reading, not the frame — nothing persists the raw
payload, by design (see the arm's comment in harness/run_loop.rs). Confirming
the wire shape against production therefore means reading the codex stderr log
or re-deriving from a newer upstream tag, not querying our own database.
